newsitem.title: ITALY: Rain may be too late to help N.Korea - U.N. agency.
newsitem.headline: Rain may be too late to help N.Korea - U.N. agency.

text.p: Rainfall over drought-stricken North Korea may have come too late to help crops already damaged by the current heat wave, the U.N. food aid agency said on Monday.
"Even if there is rain, the question is whether the rain is going to be enough to do anything," said Trevor Rowe, head of public relations at the Rome-based World Food Programme (WFP).
Rowe said assessment missions by the WFP, the agency charged with getting emergency food aid to North Korea, had shown most of the maize crops damaged by the drought were beyond recovery.
"The crops are already stunted and browned (by the sun) to such an extent that they may not be able to be saved," he said.
Official North Korean media reported over the weekend that more than 100 mm of rain fell over parts of the country on Saturday night.
Earlier reports by the communist regime's official press said the country was suffering the worst heat wave in 61 years.
The current drought comes as the reclusive state is battling to stave off famine after devastating floods in 1995-96 washed away cereal crops and left entire families without food.
The U.N.'s Food and Agriculture Agency (FAO) said on Monday it would send a mission to North Korea next week to assess damage done to crops by the latest drought.
"We will leave sometime next week and will stay for a week to 10 days," said Ajay Markanday, an FAO economist in Rome.
Markanday said maize crops in the nation's north, which borders with China, had been hit hardest by the drought, but FAO had also received reports that rice paddies were in danger.
But he said the FAO, which will undertake next week's mission together with the WFP, could not give further details at this stage.
International aid agencies have stepped up food appeals for the Stalinist state, warning of imminent starvation, especially among small children.
The WFP launched a fresh appeal earlier this month for $46 million in food aid for North Korea on top of an earlier request for $95.5 million.
